claim: Gao, Xing, Zhang (JFQA 2018): sample 1996-2010 (ends before 2015), individual-stock ATM straddles (<=60 days to expiry in the CXO summary of the working paper) bought 3 trading days before an earnings date and held to the announcement date earned a mean gross 3.34%; this is a straddle (call+put, not delta-hedged in the abstract), costs not included in the headline figure.
quote: average at-the-money straddles from 3 days before an earnings announcement to the announcement date yield a highly significant 3.34% return
title: Anticipating Uncertainty: Straddles around Earnings Announcements

claim: Same study (working-paper summary, 1996-2010, ends before 2015): delta-neutral straddles with <=60 days to expiry, moneyness 0.95-1.05, all days average gross -0.19% daily / -17.1% monthly, but net returns stay positive only for 4-10 day expiries (1.64% avg daily net, friction = half bid-ask, held 3 days before through announcement day to expiry); net profitability turns to loss as expiry lengthens or friction approaches full spread. HEDGED (delta-neutral), so not an outright buyer's return; read via CXO summary.
quote: net profitability weakens dramatically to loss as time to straddle expiration lengthens and/or trading friction approaches the bid-ask spread
title: Option Straddles Around Earnings Announcements (CXO Advisory summary of Xing & Zhang)

claim: Same study (1996-2010): gross earnings-window straddle returns were higher for small stocks, low analyst coverage, high past jump frequency, high kurtosis, large past earnings surprises, and for stocks with low implied vs realized volatility; market makers widen spreads around earnings (secondary summary).
quote: Tend to be higher for stocks with relatively high realized volatilities and relatively low implied volatilities (and therefore the smallest volatility risk premiums).
title: Option Straddles Around Earnings Announcements (CXO Advisory)

claim: Chung and Louis (J. Empirical Finance 2017): straddles purchased before earnings announcements earn positive returns, larger after low pre-formation volatility and high pre-expiration realized volatility; implied vol is overestimated after recent announcements. Sample period, maturity, hedging, costs not in abstract (full text not read).
quote: returns on straddles purchased prior to earnings announcements are actually positive
title: Earnings announcements and option returns

claim: ORATS (self-reported vendor, data to 2026-02-11): straddles on US earnings reporters averaged about 45% over the four weeks to Feb 2026 versus about -2% averaged over the prior twelve quarters; filtered for stock above $10 and option volume above 300 contracts/day; maturity, entry/exit and costs not stated; unhedged straddle presumed but not stated.
quote: options straddles on U.S. companies reporting earnings have generated an average return of approximately 45%. That compares with an average return of roughly negative 2% across the last twelve quarters.
title: Earnings Straddles Are Having Their Moment

claim: Johnson and So (JFE 2012): firms in the lowest decile of option-to-stock volume ratio outperformed the highest decile by 0.34% per week (19.3% annualized); signal stronger when short-sale costs high. Sample period, option maturity, costs not in abstract; no option position is held - it is a stock-side long/short on an option-volume signal.
quote: firms in the lowest decile of the option to stock volume ratio (O/S) outperform the highest decile by 0.34% per week (19.3% annualized)
title: The option to stock volume ratio and future returns

claim: Pan and Poteshman (RFS 2006; proprietary CBOE buyer-initiated open-volume data, sample about 1990-2001 per secondary source, ends before 2015): stocks with low put-call ratio beat high by >40bp next day and >1% next week (risk-adjusted); stock-side portfolios, not option returns.
quote: stocks with low put-call ratios outperform stocks with high put-call ratios by more than 40 basis points on the next day and more than 1% over the next week
title: The Information in Option Volume for Future Stock Prices (NBER w10925)

claim: Pan and Poteshman: the predictability comes from non-public information (the proprietary signed open-buy volume), not from publicly observable components, which the authors say predict only 1-2 days (the 1-2 day claim is from a search summary, not the cached page).
quote: the economic source of this predictability is non-public information possessed by option traders rather than market inefficiency
title: The Information in Option Volume for Future Stock Prices (NBER w10925)

claim: Baltussen et al (draft Dec 2011, via CXO summary), 1996-Oct 2009, ends before 2015: weekly-rebalanced quintile long/short on four publicly available option metrics (stocks, not options) gross 9.9% a year, but transaction costs more than offset gross profit on the wide universe; on the 100 largest stocks gross 13.6% and net 2.4% a year at 0.07% one-way friction, ignoring 0.5-1.0% a year shorting cost.
quote: A long-short strategy using the combined metrics and limited to the 100 largest stocks, with gross annual profit of 13.6% and estimated one-way trading friction of 0.07% (for large trades), generates an average net annual return of 2.4%.
title: Follow the Option Trading Leaders? (CXO summary of Baltussen et al)

claim: Hann, Kim, Zheng (Rev Accounting Studies 2019): implied volatility of peer firms moves with the first announcer's implied volatility change around its earnings announcement, stronger for long-duration options; this shows options reprice peers on read-across news, not that it is mispriced. Sample/costs not in abstract; no return measured.
quote: significantly positive association between changes in the implied volatility of each industry’s first announcer and its peers around the first announcer’s earnings announcement
title: Intra-industry information transfers: evidence from changes in implied volatility around earnings announcements

claim: Cremers and Weinbaum (JFQA 2010): stocks with relatively expensive calls (implied vol gap between call-put pairs) outperform those with expensive puts by 50bp per week; stock-side portfolios; edge fell over the sample per a search summary. Mostly an SQ2-type non-event signal; recorded as comparison.
quote: stocks with relatively expensive calls outperform stocks with relatively expensive puts by 50 basis points per week
title: Deviations from Put-Call Parity and Stock Return Predictability

claim: Barbon and Buraschi (via BSIC student summary, sample about 1996-2017): lagged aggregate dealer gamma imbalance coefficient on absolute returns is negative and highly significant for single stocks and indexes; stronger for less liquid underlyings (secondary, volatility not a return to option buyers).
quote: The results show that the coefficient of the Gamma imbalance (t-1) is negative and highly significant both for single stocks and indexes.
title: How dealers' gamma impacts underlying stocks (BSIC)

claim: OptionMetrics research post (vendor, S&P 500 options, out of sample, 2026): dealer gamma adds forecasting information for overnight gap size only in low-VIX regimes; on stressed days a HAR baseline already absorbs it. Index, not single stocks; self-reported.
quote: dealer gamma carries forecasting information about overnight gap magnitude only in low-VIX regimes
title: Dealer gamma exposure and overnight gap risk
